details: Measured 27 Oct by the speed design: relay's agent cost log (the ledger) holds 161 agent stops for that day but only 87 agent_start events, so 76 agents have no start; idle time and per-stage wall time cannot be computed from it (the design had to read the workflow transcripts instead).
failing_case: For 27 Oct, count agent_stop vs agent_start lines in the ledger: 161 vs 87.
pass_cases: Every agent the ledger records as stopped has a start event, workflow agents included.
A test feeds a workflow agent's hook input and finds both events.
The test fails with the start recording disabled.
findings.summary: The ledger misses the start of many agents

details: CONFIRMED by a count over the live ledger (read-only). The unmatched stops have exactly the keys
ts, event, session_id, cwd, agent_id, agent_type="", effort, reply_chars (about 35 chars) and no requests: the hook found no
transcript. Each id occurs once; none has any start; they fall between a tool_pre Bash and its tool_post in the same session
(e.g. 2026-10-29T00:14:31 tool_pre Bash, 00:14:35.943 agent_stop "", 00:14:42 tool_post Bash), so they are Claude Code's own
side calls during a tool call (PLAUSIBLE: the auto-mode permission classifier), not agents anyone started. The change's
comment ("Claude Code sends no SubagentStart for many agents (workflow agents included)") misreads the cause: real agents
without a start are 1-2 a day. The brief's pass case "Every agent the ledger records as stopped has a start event" is
therefore not met, and the speed design's idle/wall-time numbers still see some 220 phantom stops a day.
evidence: python3 count over ~/.relay/ledger/2026-10-2{7,8,9}.jsonl, stops whose agent_id has no agent_start, keyed by (has run, agent_type, has requests):
keys of all 222: ('agent_id','agent_type','cwd','effort','event','reply_chars','session_id','ts'); empty-type stops with a start: 0
failing_case: Hook input, with no SubagentStart before it (the shape of 222 of 222 unmatched stops on 29 Oct):
Now: the ledger holds one agent_stop for a780b64f2dad9b91b and no agent_start (path is None, so the new code never runs).
Item's failing case after the change, replayed on live data: 29 Oct 740 stops vs 520 starts, 222 stops unmatched, all of this
shape; 28 Oct 440 unmatched, 438 of this shape, 2 workflow runners (the only ones the change fixes); 27 Oct 218, 217 of this shape.
Should: no agent_stop is left without an agent_start in the same session (pass case 1 of the item).
fix_hint: In the SubagentStop branch, when no agent transcript is found and agent_type is empty, record the line as a separate event
(e.g. "side_call", keeping reply_chars) instead of agent_stop, so it neither counts as an agent nor needs a start; keep the
synthetic start for real agents. Add the test of pass case 1 and 4, and correct the code comment's stated cause.
pass_cases: 1. The input above (empty agent_type, no transcript found, no prior SubagentStart) -> the ledger holds no agent_stop for
a780b64f2dad9b91b without an agent_start for it (either it is recorded under another event name, e.g. "side_call",
or a start is written with it); a test asserts the count of unmatched agent_stop lines is 0.
2. Workflow agent: SubagentStop with agent_transcript_path .../workflows/wf_abc/agent-w1.jsonl (first line 2026-10-19T10:00:00Z),
no start -> exactly one agent_start for w1 with ts 2026-10-19T10:00:00Z and one agent_stop (the existing new test).
3. SubagentStart a1 (delegate:scout) then SubagentStop a1 with transcript -> exactly one agent_start, one agent_stop with requests 1.
4. A stop with a non-empty agent_type (delegate:runner) and no transcript found -> still recorded as agent_stop with reply_chars
(whatever the fix does to side calls must not hide real agents).
findings.summary: the stops that lack a start are almost all transcript-less side calls with an empty agent_type; the fix needs a transcript, so the item's count barely moves (29 Oct: 0 of 222 fixed)

details: CONFIRMED by reading. Cost is small (two full scans of the 4.8 MB 29 Oct file: 12 ms), so correctness is fine today; the
docstring is the stated contract of "must never slow a session" and is now wrong. Size: 5 minutes.
evidence: timing: two full scans of ~/.relay/ledger/2026-10-29.jsonl -> 12 ms
failing_case: A workflow agent stop on the same day as its start, no SubagentStart: has_start(aid, started, ts) opens and scans the same
4.8 MB day file twice; the docstring (lines 9-13) says the only files read besides stdin are a transcript tail and 4 KB of
.meta.json. Should: the docstring names the day-file scan, and one day is scanned once.
fix_hint: Dedupe the day files in has_start (a set of day_file paths) and add one line to the docstring.
pass_cases: 1. Docstring of ledger.py lists the day-file scan on SubagentStop among the files read.
3. has_start over a start day and a different stop day still finds a start written in either day file.
reason: test_has_start_scans_each_day_file_once_and_finds_either_day passes, fails without the fix; docstring updated.
findings.summary: the module docstring still promises the hook reads only a transcript tail and 4 KB of meta; it now scans whole day files, twice when both stamps fall on one day
